interest: This file provides valuable insight into Japanese cultural diplomacy and soft-power strategies in Latin America on the eve of World War II, specifically how Japan's Department of Tourism within the Ministry of Railway Transportation sought to cultivate influence among prominent Brazilian intellectuals. It is particularly interesting in highlighting the caliber of academics targeted—including Dr. Geraldo de Paula Souza, a key public health figure closely linked with the American Rockefeller Foundation—and illustrates American consular surveillance of Japanese propaganda, language education, and diaspora activities in São Paulo during the Vargas era.
overview: This file consists of two despatches sent in July and August 1939 by Carol H. Foster, U.S. Consul General in São Paulo, Brazil, to Jefferson Caffery, the U.S. Ambassador to Brazil in Rio de Janeiro, reporting on Japanese cultural propaganda initiatives and educational outreach. The communications document an initiative announced by Japanese Consul General Junzo Sakané on behalf of the Department of Tourism of the Japanese Ministry of Railway Transportation to invite five Brazilian university professors on an all-expenses-paid visit to Japan as official guests. Consul General Foster details the selection of two distinguished faculty members from the University of São Paulo—Dr. Geraldo de Paula Souza from the Faculty of Medicine (and director of the Institute of Hygiene) and Dr. Soares de Mello from the Faculty of Law—while also assessing the limited success of Japanese language courses at the São Paulo Law School and tracking the registration of 47 Japanese teachers in the state.

subfiles.about: Reports on a Japanese government initiative to invite five Brazilian university professors to Japan, as well as the status of Japanese language instruction and registered Japanese teachers in São Paulo.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Carol H. Foster reports to Ambassador Jefferson Caffery on an announcement by Japanese Consul General Junzo Sakané regarding an official invitation from the Department of Tourism of the Japanese Ministry of Railway Transportation for five Brazilian university professors to visit Japan, including representatives from the University of São Paulo's law and medical faculties. Foster observes that free Japanese language courses offered at the São Paulo Law School appear to be struggling to attract students. He also notes, citing the Folha da Noite and the Directory of Teaching, that 47 Japanese teachers were officially registered in São Paulo.
subfiles.title: Letter from Consul General Foster to Ambassador Caffery on Japanese Propaganda and Invitation to Brazilian Professors

subfiles.about: Identifies the two professors from the University of São Paulo selected to visit Japan as guests of the Japanese government.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Foster updates Ambassador Caffery that the two professors from the University of São Paulo invited to Japan have been selected: Dr. Geraldo de Paula Souza of the Faculty of Medicine and Dr. Soares de Mello of the Faculty of Law. They are scheduled to travel to Rio de Janeiro to join other Brazilian professors participating in the Japanese-sponsored tour. Foster notes Dr. de Paula Souza's significant ties with the Rockefeller Foundation through the Institute of Hygiene and Dr. Soares de Mello's representation of Brazil at the previous year's Congress of Criminology in Rome.
subfiles.title: Letter from Consul General Foster to Ambassador Caffery on Paulista Professors Invited to Japan
